title: Identity and composition for tensor-formula module pullback
statement: Let $X,Y,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $g:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to Z$ morphisms, and for any morphism $a:A\to B$ among them let $P_a:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_B)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_A)$ be the pullback functor whose value on a sheaf of modules $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is $P_a\mathcal G=\mathcal O_A\otimes_{a^{-1}\mathcal O_B}a^{-1}\mathcal G$, using inverse image of sheaves [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] and the sheaf tensor product/change of rings [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and whose action on morphisms is induced by inverse image and tensor product. Then there are natural isomorphisms of functors $P_{\mathrm{id}_X}\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)}$ and $P_{h\circ g}\cong P_g\circ P_h$.

source.place: Tag 0097, lemma-push-pull-composition-modules (lines 3189-3202), with the identity case from Tag 0095, definition-pushforward (lines 3116-3141) and uniqueness of left adjoints used in the proof of lemma-pullback-composition (lines 2209-2223)

proof.text: For the identity morphism $\mathrm{id}_X$, the sectionwise pushforward in [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] is the identity functor on $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$: both the inverse image on opens and restriction of scalars along the identity ring map are identities. The same node gives $P_{\mathrm{id}_X}\dashv\mathrm{id}$. The identity functor is left adjoint to itself with its identity unit and counit [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The canonical uniqueness isomorphism between left adjoints, applied to these two adjunctions, therefore gives $P_{\mathrm{id}_X}\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)}$.

source.place: Tag 0095, definition-pushforward, lines 3116-3152, together with the identity-adjunction argument used in Tag 0097's pullback proof (lines 3197-3202)

proof.text: For $g:X\to Y$ and $h:Y\to Z$, the sectionwise definition of pushforward gives $(h\circ g)_*=h_*\circ g_*$: on an open $W\subseteq Z$ both sides evaluate a module on $(h\circ g)^{-1}(W)=g^{-1}(h^{-1}(W))$, and the module action is restricted along the same composite ring map. By [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction], $P_g\dashv g_*$ and $P_h\dashv h_*$. Their composite adjunction, whose left adjoint is $P_g\circ P_h$ and right adjoint is $h_*\circ g_*$, is [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Thus $P_{h\circ g}$ and $P_g\circ P_h$ are left adjoints to the same functor; the canonical uniqueness isomorphism of left adjoints gives the required natural isomorphism $P_{h\circ g}\cong P_g\circ P_h$.
